name: Netherlands
summary: The Netherlands does not tax dividends and capital gains on a private portfolio as such. Instead, Box 3 taxes a deemed return on net assets held on 1 January at 36%: for 2026 the deemed return on investments is 6.00%, so a securities portfolio costs 2.16% of its value each year above a tax-free EUR 59,357 per person, which works as a wealth tax. Taxpayers may report a lower actual return (including unrealised gains) instead. A new actual-return system is expected from 1 January 2028. Shareholdings of 5% or more are taxed in Box 2 at up to 31%. Children pay inheritance and gift tax of 10% on the first EUR 158,669 and 20% above, after a EUR 26,230 inheritance exemption (2026).

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents are taxed on worldwide income in three boxes: Box 1 (work and home, up to 49.5%), Box 2 (substantial interests of 5% or more, 24.5%/31%), Box 3 (savings and investments, deemed return taxed at 36%).
regimes.eligibility: Residence determined by all facts and circumstances (art. 4 AWR): durable personal ties such as a permanent home and family. Non-EU citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: No separate capital gains tax on portfolio shares, bonds or investment real estate: they sit in Box 3, which taxes a deemed annual return on their value (see wealth tax). Gains on a substantial interest (5% or more of a company, alone or with partner/close relatives) are taxed in Box 2 at 24.5% on the first EUR 68,843 and 31% above (2026). The main home is in Box 1 and its sale is not taxed.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Box 3 allowance EUR 59,357 per person (2026), applied to the wealth base, not to gains.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Under the planned actual-return system (expected 1 January 2028) Box 3 would tax actual returns at 36%, including unrealised value changes on most listed assets (capital-gains-style for real estate and start-up shares); not in force. Box 2 exit tax: emigrating holders of a substantial interest get a protective assessment on the unrealised gain (from general knowledge).

sources.title: Netherlands - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Box 2 protective assessment on emigration was not re-verified.
Parliamentary status of the actual-return bill (Wet werkelijk rendement box 3) as of October 2026: the Belastingdienst says 'likely' 1 January 2028.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Portfolio securities and investment real estate: 0 because realised gains are not taxed separately; their value is taxed annually through Box 3 (recorded under wealth_tax). Private business sale (>= 5%): Box 2 top rate 31%. Headline = the Box 2 top rate. Foreign real estate is in Box 3 but most treaties exempt it with progression.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading activity that goes beyond normal asset management ('meer dan normaal vermogensbeheer') moves results into Box 1 (result from other activities) at up to 49.5%; leveraged or highly active trading carries this risk.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide assets in Box 3; foreign real estate usually exempt under treaties or unilateral relief (with progression).

dividends.summary: Portfolio dividends are not taxed as income: they are part of the Box 3 deemed return. Dutch dividends bear 15% dividend withholding tax, which a resident credits against income tax. Foreign withholding tax can be credited against the Box 3 tax under treaties and the unilateral decree (limited). Dividends from a substantial interest (5%+) are taxed in Box 2 at 24.5%/31%.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Resident individual; holdings below 5% for Box 3 treatment.
dividends.important_exceptions: If the taxpayer opts for the actual return, dividends received count toward it.

sources.title: Netherlands - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: How far foreign dividend withholding tax can be credited against Box 3 tax (treaty credit limited to the Box 3 tax attributable to that income) was not verified.
dividends.rate_basis: Portfolio dividends: 0 as separate income tax (the asset value is taxed via Box 3 under wealth_tax). Headline: Box 2 top rate 31% for substantial interests.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% dividend withholding tax on dividends paid by Dutch companies, reduced by treaties and to 0% for qualifying EU/treaty corporate parents; a conditional withholding tax applies to payments to low-tax jurisdictions.
dividends.treaty_network: About 95 income tax treaties, including the US and all EU states (count from general knowledge).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the structure regime 'beleggings_bv': moving the portfolio into a BV takes it out of Box 3 (2.16% a year on its value); the BV pays 19%/25.8% on actual realised dividends and gains (no participation exemption below 5%), and distributions are taxed in Box 2 at 24.5%/31%.

wealth_tax.summary: Box 3 works as a wealth tax. On net assets held on 1 January (main home excluded) the law deems a return of 6.00% on investments and other assets, 1.28% on bank deposits (provisional) and -2.70% on debts (provisional) for 2026; the deemed return on the part above the allowance of EUR 59,357 per person (EUR 118,714 for partners) is taxed at 36%. For a securities portfolio that is 2.16% of its value a year. If the actual return (income plus realised and unrealised value changes, no allowance) is lower, the taxpayer can report it in the return and pay 36% of that instead.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 59,357 per person (2026); debts only count above EUR 3,800 per person. Children have their own allowance if they hold assets.
wealth_tax.eligibility_conditions: Resident individuals on worldwide assets; non-residents only on certain Dutch assets.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Rebuttal: since Supreme Court rulings (2021, 2024) the tax may not exceed 36% of the actual return; the Wet tegenbewijsregeling box 3 lets taxpayers prove a lower actual return. A new Box 3 with taxation of actual returns is expected from 1 January 2028 (not in force). From 2026 own use of a second home is added to the actual return.
open_questions: The deposit and debt percentages for 2026 are provisional until early 2027; the 6.00% for investments is final.
The schema cannot express the 'lower of deemed or actual return' rule; in a year with a portfolio return below 6% the real tax is lower than modelled.

components.name: Box 3 deemed return tax on investments (6.00% x 36%)
components.notes: Effective annual rate 6.00% deemed return x 36% = 2.16% on investments above the allowance of EUR 118,714 for a couple (EUR 59,357 each). Bank deposits: 1.28% x 36% = 0.46%; debts reduce the base at 2.70%. Main home excluded (Box 1). Foreign real estate usually exempt under treaties.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal property tax (OZB) on the WOZ value, usually around 0.1% a year for owners of homes; the main home is also taxed in Box 1 through a notional rental value (eigenwoningforfait).

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax is charged on each heir. In 2026 a child has an exemption of EUR 26,230; the rest is taxed at 10% up to EUR 158,669 and 20% above. A spouse or partner has an exemption of EUR 828,035. The tax applies if the deceased lived in the Netherlands; Dutch nationals remain treated as resident for 10 years after emigrating, and for gift tax anyone remains resident for one year after leaving.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Child EUR 26,230 (2026); disabled child EUR 78,671; partner EUR 828,035. Gift tax: annual exemption for gifts from parents to children and a one-off increased exemption (for a home, study or freely between ages 18 and 39), amounts not verified for 2026.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Deceased or donor resident (or deemed resident) in the Netherlands at the time of the transfer; non-resident donors/deceased are not taxed even on Dutch assets.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Business succession facility (BOR): large exemption for qualifying business assets, not for investment assets; the BOR has been tightened in recent budgets (2025/2026 details not verified).
open_questions: The 10-year (Dutch nationals) and 1-year (gifts) residence fictions (art. 3 SW 1956) and the gift exemptions for 2026 were not checked on an official page (Belastingdienst gift pages returned 404).
BOR changes in the 2026 budget were not verified.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gift tax uses the same rates (10% / 20% for children) with smaller exemptions: an annual exemption for gifts from parents to a child and a one-off higher exemption; gifts from the same donor in one calendar year are aggregated. Gifts made within 180 days before death are added to the estate.
inheritance.business_relief: BOR (bedrijfsopvolgingsregeling): 100% exemption up to a cap and 83% above for qualifying business assets with continuation conditions; investment assets and listed portfolios do not qualify.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Worldwide estate if the deceased was resident or deemed resident; credit or exemption for foreign tax under the unilateral decree and the few estate tax treaties.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Dutch nationals who die within 10 years of leaving the Netherlands are treated as resident; anyone who makes a gift within one year of leaving is treated as resident for gift tax. The heir's residence does not matter.
inheritance.spouse_note: A partner (spouse, registered or cohabiting partner) has an exemption of EUR 828,035 in 2026; the rest is taxed at 10% up to EUR 158,669 and 20% above (Successiewet 1956), about 20% effective on a EUR 35M estate.

regimes.name: Investment BV (beleggings-BV)
regimes.description: The family holds the portfolio through a Dutch BV owned by the parents. Their shares in the BV are a substantial interest (at least 5%), taxed in Box 2 only when money comes out, so the portfolio leaves Box 3 and its 2.16% annual deemed-return tax. The BV pays corporate income tax on its actual realised income: 19% on the first EUR 200,000 and 25.8% above, on portfolio dividends and gains alike (the participation exemption needs a 5% stake). Distributions are taxed in Box 2 at 24.5%/31%. Inheritance tax is the same as for direct holding (business succession relief does not cover investment assets), so that metric is inherited from the standard regime.
regimes.eligibility: Any Dutch resident can set up a BV (no minimum capital; notarial deed). Moving a Box 3 portfolio into the BV triggers no income tax (Box 3 has no capital gains tax), so existing holdings can be contributed at market value.
regimes.duration_note: A corporate structure under ordinary law with no time limit. Its comparative advantage depends on Box 3: the planned actual-return Box 3 (expected from 2028, not in force) would tax unrealised gains annually at 36%, which would widen the BV's advantage.

structure.payout_notes: Dividends to the parents are Box 2 income: 24.5% on the first EUR 68,843 per person and 31% above (2026, art. 2.12 Wet IB 2001); partners can split Box 2 income, so two parents use the lower band twice (on EUR 400,000 about 28.8% overall; the top rate 31% is used here). The BV withholds 15% Dutch dividend tax, credited against Box 2. Loans from the BV above EUR 500,000 per shareholder (with partner), other than qualifying home loans, are taxed as a deemed Box 2 dividend (excessive borrowing rule).
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Portfolio shares (stakes below 5%) do not qualify for the participation exemption, so dividends and gains are fully taxed at 19%/25.8%; foreign withholding tax is credited under treaties (or deducted as a cost). No exit or lock-in at company level, but the excessive-borrowing rule blocks tax-free access to the money through loans. The fiscal investment institution (FBI, 0% corporate tax with a distribution obligation) has shareholder restrictions that were not verified for a single family. Shares in the BV are Box 2 assets, not Box 3 assets, so they are outside the deemed-return tax.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Emigration: the Netherlands issues a protective assessment on the Box 2 gain built up in the BV shares; payment can be deferred under conditions. Death: the shares are deemed disposed of (Box 2 tax at 31% on the gain), unless the heirs roll the latent claim over (art. 4.17a Wet IB 2001), which needs an enterprise in the company; district courts have refused it for BVs without one (see the regime's inheritance entry). Liquidation: distributions above paid-in capital are Box 2 income at 24.5%/31%.

capital_gains.summary: The BV pays corporate income tax on realised gains on portfolio shares and bonds: 19% on the first EUR 200,000 of taxable profit and 25.8% above (2026). Unrealised gains are not taxed. Gains on a stake of at least 5% in a private company are exempt under the participation exemption (if it is not a low-taxed portfolio investment).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Participation exemption for stakes of at least 5%; none for portfolio holdings.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Unlike Box 3, the BV is taxed on actual realised income, so a year with low or negative returns costs little. Rates in the model are the 25.8% top rate; the 19% band on the first EUR 200,000 lowers the average slightly.

wealth_tax.summary: No Box 3 deemed-return tax on the portfolio: the parents' shares in the BV are a substantial interest taxed in Box 2, and the BV itself has no net wealth tax. Savings and investments kept outside the BV stay in Box 3; the family home is in Box 1.
wealth_tax.eligibility_conditions: Shareholding of at least 5% in the BV (substantial interest).
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: The 2.16% Box 3 charge is replaced by corporate tax on realised income plus Box 2 tax on distributions.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal OZB on the home as in the standard regime.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax as for direct holding, on the value of the BV shares (10%/20% for children above EUR 26,230 each). In addition the death is a deemed disposal of the parents' substantial interest (art. 4.16 lid 1 letter e Wet IB 2001): Box 2 income tax at 31% (24.5% on the first EUR 68,843) on the shares' value above the parents' acquisition price. The roll-over (doorschuiving, art. 4.17a Wet IB 2001) needs an enterprise in the company; for a BV holding only a listed portfolio, district courts have refused it.

inheritance.important_exceptions: Business succession facility (BOR): large exemption for qualifying business assets, not for investment assets; the BOR has been tightened in recent budgets (2025/2026 details not verified).

residency.tax_residency_test: Facts and circumstances (art. 4 General Taxation Act): durable personal ties such as a permanent home, family, registration and intended stay. As a rule of thumb an expatriate whose family moves with them is resident from arrival.

corporate.summary: Corporate income tax 19% on the first EUR 200,000 and 25.8% above. Participation exemption for holdings of at least 5%. Dividend withholding tax 15%; conditional withholding tax on payments to low-tax jurisdictions.

us_citizen_notes: US-Netherlands income tax treaty and the 1969 US-Netherlands estate tax treaty apply. Box 3 tax on a deemed return is generally not creditable as a foreign income tax against US tax on actual dividends and gains (no matching income), so US citizens can face both.
open_questions: 30% ruling: an employment-income regime (30% tax-free allowance, falling to 27% from 2027). The partial non-resident status that kept Box 3 off worldwide assets was abolished from 2025, with grandfathering to the end of 2026 only for people who used it before 2024, so it gives a new arrival no Box 3 relief and is not modelled.
Actual-return Box 3 expected from 2028; when enacted, CGT and dividend fields will need real rates (36% on actual returns).
Residence routes for non-EU nationals not verified.
